title: The optical force on a dielectric slab
authors: Andrew Laeuger, Kevin Kuns, Yanbei Chen, Nancy Aggarwal
abstract: Radiation-pressure forces on transmissive optics, including dynamical backaction, are usually computed from the momentum flux of the external fields. For a dielectric of finite thickness, this omits the time dependence of the electromagnetic momentum stored inside. We compute the force on a lossless dielectric slab of arbitrary thickness $L_s$ submerged in a dielectric fluid, proceeding from both Lorentz force on its bound charges and from the external momentum fluxes for arbitrary carrier and sideband fields. We treat the surrounding medium through a prescribed linear dielectric response and do not model the accompanying mechanical response of the fluid, including pressure and electrostriction. These two methods both recover the expected force in the limit of a thin reflector, but differ in the more general case by the rate of change of the field momentum stored in the slab. This storage term vanishes for static fields and at low frequencies reduces to $(L_s/c^2)\,dP/dt$, where $P$ is the net power through the slab. In a cavity, where $P$ depends on the slab position, the storage term produces a velocity-dependent force. The Abraham and Minkowski momentum formulations applied to the storage term are reconciled to give an unambiguous force on the dielectric in the case of an exterior vacuum environment, where there is no fluid response to model.
summary: This theoretical work develops a comprehensive method to calculate the optical force on a dielectric slab by comparing the Lorentz force approach with momentum flux conservation. The key finding is that accounting for the time-dependent electromagnetic momentum stored inside the slab is necessary to reconcile conflicting results from different theoretical frameworks. This has implications for accurately modeling forces in optical cavities and optomechanical systems.
main_problem: The paper addresses the accurate calculation of the optical force exerted on a dielectric slab, specifically resolving discrepancies arising from the time dependence of electromagnetic momentum stored within the slab.
main_result: The force calculation must incorporate a 'storage term' related to the time rate of change of stored field momentum to reconcile different theoretical formulations (Lorentz vs. momentum flux).
method: The authors employ two primary theoretical approaches—calculating the force via the Lorentz force on bound charges and via external momentum fluxes—and compare these results against continuum formulations (Minkowski and Abraham).
model_or_system: The system is a lossless, linear dielectric slab of arbitrary thickness submerged in a dielectric fluid, interacting with incident and reflected optical fields, often analyzed using a two-photon formalism.
key_observables: Optical force ($\vec{F}$), momentum flux ($\vec{g}$), stress tensor ($\vec{\sigma}$), and the storage term ($ rac{d\vec{p}_{	ext{vac}}}{dt}$).
important_parameters: Slab thickness ($L_s$), refractive indices ($n_1, n_2$), and the frequency dependence (DC vs. AC fields).
main_assumptions: The surrounding medium is treated via a prescribed linear dielectric response, neglecting the accompanying mechanical response (pressure, electrostriction) of the fluid.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the decomposition of the electric field into carrier and sideband components on either side of the slab interfaces.
paper_structure: The paper methodically compares the results from the Lorentz force calculation against those derived from momentum flux conservation, focusing on how the inclusion of the internal field momentum storage term resolves discrepancies between different continuum formulations.
why_interesting: The rigorous reconciliation of different momentum formulations (Abraham vs. Minkowski) by identifying the role of stored field momentum is crucial for accurately modeling forces in cavity QED and optomechanics where field dynamics are central.
